claims.claim: The same reviewer says that layered unreliability is not done in an intrusive, postmodern way and was subliminal enough that he missed it on a first reading.
claims.source: Vacuous Wastrel blog, review of The Golden Fool
claims.quote: It’s not done in an intrusive, postmodern way
claims.page: review of 'The Golden Fool, by Robin Hobb', final discussion paragraph

claims.claim: The same reviewer describes Hobb's language as carrying a slightly heavy and old-fashioned tone common to the genre, while still delivering memorable lines.
claims.source: Vacuous Wastrel blog, review of Fool's Quest
claims.quote: slightly heavy and old-fashioned tone common to the genre
claims.page: review of Fool's Quest, Overall section

claims.claim: The same reviewer dissents from the general praise of Hobb's prose, calling it unremarkable and saying the flashes of beautiful imagery are balanced by her willingness to describe the horrific and the ugly.
claims.source: Vacuous Wastrel blog, review of a later Elderlings novel
claims.quote: As is usually the case with Hobb, her prose is unremarkable

claims.claim: Novelist M Harold Page states a rule he derives from Fool's Assassin: Hobb delivers description only when it is part of a conflict, giving the fashionable trousers being argued over as his example.
claims.source: M Harold Page, Black Gate, 9 February 2016
claims.quote: She only delivers description when it’s part of a conflict

claims.claim: Page states a second rule: Hobb serves up characterisation at the moment it bears on a choice or tactic, illustrating with a stable hand who might teach the narrator to ride.
claims.source: M Harold Page, Black Gate, 9 February 2016
claims.quote: Hobb always serves up characterisation when it is immediately significant

claims.claim: Page identifies an unremitting rhythm of the word but at every level of Fool's Assassin, so that nothing in the book arrives without a qualification.
claims.source: M Harold Page, Black Gate, 9 February 2016
claims.quote: an unremitting rhythm of buts at all levels
claims.page: section 'Making Lyrical Fantasy Interesting', first bullet

claims.claim: Page says the qualifications nest inside one another at several scales, calling Hobb's buts fractal.
claims.source: M Harold Page, Black Gate, 9 February 2016
claims.page: section 'Making Lyrical Fantasy Interesting', first bullet

claims.claim: Page states the braiding rule he finds in Fool's Assassin: a death arising from the thriller plot carries domestic and child-rearing implications, and a death in the domestic plot sets off the thriller.
claims.source: M Harold Page, Black Gate, 9 February 2016
claims.quote: a death resulting from the Thriller has domestic and child-rearing implications
claims.page: section 'First Person Slow Burn Thriller', bullet on braiding

claims.claim: Page says Hobb links the domestic and political plots practically and not only thematically, the same duty manifesting in both.
claims.source: M Harold Page, Black Gate, 9 February 2016
claims.quote: the same duty manifests both domestically and politically

claims.claim: Page describes Hobb's substitute for a viewpoint shift in a first-person thriller: information is dropped after the fact but in a way that points forward.
claims.source: M Harold Page, Black Gate, 9 February 2016
claims.quote: She drops information on us after-the-fact but in ways that point forward

claims.claim: Page notes that the retrospective narrator's editorialising is confined to bookending episodes so that it does not break the flow of the narrative.
claims.source: M Harold Page, Black Gate, 9 February 2016
claims.quote: only to bookend episodes, and does not break the flow
